text:
owen park: Hey team, first-week puzzle. I started the postgres container from the repo root with `docker compose up -d db` and then in the api folder ran `docker compose up --build api`. The api container can't resolve `db` — error: "could not translate host name "db"". Both containers are running but DNS/name resolution is failing. Any idea?

owen park: I tried pinging `db` from the api container and it can't find it. I'm on mac, using Docker Desktop stable.

julia nguyen: welcome owen! sounds like the two compose runs are creating separate compose projects and networks. By default `docker compose` uses the directory name as the project name, so running from two different folders makes two isolated networks where service names don't cross-resolve.

sam cole: yep. check with `docker compose ps` in each folder and `docker network ls` to see networks. If you see networks like `repo_root_default` and `api_default`, containers are on different networks. Use a common network or run both services from the same compose invocation.

owen park: I see two networks. What are practical fixes? I don't want to move files around.

julia nguyen: options: 1) start both services from a single compose invocation (preferred for dev), e.g. from repo root `docker compose up --build db api`; 2) use an external network: create a network `docker network create redwood-dev` and in both compose files declare the external network and attach services to it so names resolve across projects; 3) set an explicit project name so both runs share the same project/network, e.g. `docker compose -p redwood-dev up` in both folders.

sam cole: quick example for external network in compose: 
```yaml
networks:
  redwood-dev:
    external: true
services:
  db:
    networks: [redwood-dev]
  api:
    networks: [redwood-dev]
```
Then `docker network create redwood-dev` once. That lets `api` resolve `db` by service name across folders.

owen park: nice. I tried `docker compose -p redwood-dev up` in both directories and now `ping db` from api works. One thing: I had leftover containers with the old project name; do I need to cleanup?

julia nguyen: good practice to prune old unused compose projects: `docker compose -p oldproj down` from the old folder or `docker rm` the stray containers. `docker network prune` can remove unused networks, but be careful if others use them. `docker ps -a` shows old containers.

sam cole: also watch port mappings: if both projects tried to bind host ports (e.g., `5432:5432`) the second attempt would fail. Using internal networking without ports is safer for inter-container comms; only map ports when you need host access.

owen park: thanks all 1 that fixed it. I'll update my workflow notes: prefer a shared project name for multi-repo compose runs or use an external network. Also removing host port bindings for inter-container comms helped avoid collisions.

devex-bot: Tip: onboarding doc updated with a short section on compose project names and external networks: https://redwood.internal/devenv/compose-projects. If you want a one-line helper to bring everything up from monorepo root, ping #devex for the script.

owen park: closing this out 1 appreciate the fast help! :raised_hands:
